gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-julius-sans-one: Commanding letters stretch wide across the line in Amadeus, with generous gaps between curve ends and stems. Amadeus makes the statement; Julius Sans One lets its open curves breathe.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads as if drawn with one nib, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. Wide, commanding Amadeus leads the page while that body keeps everything approachable.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-gambetta: Azonix keeps capitals barely above lowercase, so words need a moment. Azonix commands with wide, crisp shapes even when shrunk, while Gambetta, the serif, draws gently shifting strokes into open counters.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-epilogue: Heavy, cord-like curves and a wide-open e give Brusher its dynamic, calligraphic hand. Epilogue stays slim and wire-like, with stubby ascender tips on a tall-bodied lowercase whose curves feel pleasantly unclamped.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-fira-sans: Brusher writes in a calligraphic hand, its curves as bold as its stems. The standout quality is the jump from rope-like romance to Fira Sans, whose wide-open s curves and large x-height read plainly.
gen-dafont-brusher-manrope: Manrope reads bright and clean, with an open gap at every curve's mouth and barely any step from capitals to lowercase. Brusher adds a romantic, calligraphic flourish to that quiet clarity.
gen-dafont-brusher-montserrat: Romantic and dynamic, Brusher writes in a calligraphic hand with curves heavy as cord and a wide-open e. Montserrat sends paragraphs gliding by like wire, white space leading into each curve.
gen-dafont-brusher-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its c tips well apart and its mean line set high, a contemporary, modern text face. Brusher adds romance with a calligraphic hand and cord-heavy curves.
gen-dafont-cheri-bitter: Cheri is inviting and cute, a calligraphic hand whose tall lowercase looks sturdy. Where Cheri charms with hairline-free curves, Bitter, the slab-serif, grounds the text with a see-through gap in each s.
gen-dafont-cheri-mulish: No hairlines, so Cheri gives every stem and curve the same heft. Cheri does the inviting with tall, sturdy words, while Mulish, the sans, offers horseshoe-open curves and short ascenders.
